title: Burst correlation matrix — token/QPS by market & headroom implications
summary: Objective: quantify cross-market burst correlation to optimize pooled vs regional-dedicated safety headroom. This sheet decomposes historical peak windows into a correlation matrix (markets = NA-US, NA-EU, APAC, LATAM), derives joint-probability of simultaneous peaks, and converts that into conservative headroom targets (tokens/sec and QPS) per region and for a pooled global ingress allocation.
assumptions:
- Historical window: 2025-01-01 to 2026-06-30 (15m and 1h buckets)
- Token definition: generation tokens (not counting prompt-only embed calls)
- Peak definition: 95th percentile 15-minute bucket per market
- Baseline model mix: 70% dense-chat-class, 20% long-form-generation, 10% embeddings for this workload
- Average tokens per request by class: dense-chat 120, long-form 850, embeddings 1
- GPU throughput baseline: H100 80k tokens/sec (mixed seq), A100 45k tokens/sec (mixed seq)
scenarios: Scenario A — Localized peaks: 3 markets peak independently; low cross-correlation (rho ~0.2); safe to rely on 20% pooled buffer
Scenario B — Synchronized marketing event: NA+EU simultaneous peaks (rho ~0.6) for 2 hours; requires extra regional reservation or cross-region burst capacity
Scenario C — Global outage retry storm: High correlation across all markets (rho ~0.85) in 5–30 minute microbursts; worst-case planning scenario
correlation_matrix_summary: Computed pairwise Pearson correlations on 15-minute token series aggregated by market. Key takeaways: NA-US vs NA-EU = 0.62 (weekday business hours overlap), NA-US vs APAC = 0.28, NA-EU vs APAC = 0.31, APAC vs LATAM = 0.12. Joint tail probability (all four >95th) is low (~0.6% historically) but rises to ~4.2% during product launches and marketing pushes.
numeric_headroom_targets:
Recommended headroom targets (conservative):
- NA-US: baseline peak=210k tokens/sec (95p 15m) -> target headroom = +32% -> provisioning target = 276k tokens/sec (approx 3.45k QPS assuming 80 tokens/req mix)
- NA-EU: baseline peak=155k tokens/sec -> headroom +30% -> provisioning = 202k tokens/sec (~2.5k QPS)
- APAC: baseline peak=98k tokens/sec -> headroom +40% (higher variance) -> provisioning = 137k tokens/sec (~1.6k QPS)
- LATAM: baseline peak=32k tokens/sec -> headroom +50% (low capacity, high spike uncertainty) -> provisioning = 48k tokens/sec (~600 QPS)
Global pooled emergency buffer (cross-region fungible capacity): target = 180k tokens/sec reserved for correlated events (covers historical joint spikes up to 99th conditional percentile).
gpu_pool_mix_recommendation:
Translate tokens -> GPU slices (conservative): assume H100 equiv throughput = 80k tokens/sec; A100 equiv = 45k tokens/sec. Target pool (regional):
- NA-US: 2 H100 + 2 A100 (hot pool) + 1 H100 warm spare -> effective ~ (2*80 + 2*45) = 250k tokens/sec hot capacity -> aligns with 276k target when accounting for KV cache warming and prewarm latency.
- NA-EU: 2 A100 + 1 H100 -> ~170k tokens/sec hot; add flexible pooled H100 from global buffer as needed.
- APAC: 1 H100 + 1 A100 -> ~125k tokens/sec hot; add prewarm slices during business hours.
- LATAM: 1 A100 with aggressive autoscale to pooled GPU slices.
Notes: prefer H100 for dense-chat tails; A100 for steady medium-latency workloads. Use quantized variants and batching config to push effective throughput up ~15% in steady-state.
prewarm_strategy:
Heuristics:
- 15m rolling increase > 18% above baseline -> trigger thin prewarm (bring 1 warm H100 slice online)
- 30m sustained increase > 30% -> trigger thick prewarm (additional A100/H100 per region depending on mix)
- Cross-region failover: if correlated probability estimate > 0.5 for next 1h (based on event signals), warm global pooled H100s ahead of time.
Operational notes: prewarm ops should use 'graceful-holder' mode to avoid premature token consumption; aim for <20s cold-start to first token for warmed slices. Track prewarm cost vs avoided SLO breaches weekly.
